ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are two terminals; the upper terminal first connects to an inductor labeled L, the circuit then goes downward along the right side through a capacitor labeled C, and finally returns to the lower-left terminal through the lower wire, so this is a two-terminal series L-C circuit. Reasoning: Given f=50 Hz, L=3/314 H, C=1/314 F. The angular frequency ω=2πf≈314 rad/s. The inductive reactance X_L=ωL=314×(3/314)=3 Ω; the capacitive reactance X_C=1/(ωC)=1/(314×1/314)=1 Ω. The impedance of the series LC is Z=j(X_L-X_C)=j(3-1)=j2 Ω, so the impedance magnitude |Z|=2 Ω.
